name: Japanese Pork Katsu Curry Rice
tuning: RICH-DISH FLAG: still >900 after trim - manual balance in spec phase
intro_html: Crispy breaded pork cutlets sliced over rice and blanketed in glossy Japanese curry sauce. This is the splurge bowl of the section, built big on purpose: 51 grams of protein and 953 calories for about $3.87 (at everyday cost). Save it for the hungriest week on your calendar.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (black pepper, salt): ~$1.21. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $47.91 across 14 servings, so roughly $3.42 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $51.66 across 14 servings, roughly $3.69 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $9.58 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $61.24. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $3.87 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a katsu curry plate that runs $16 at a Japanese restaurant, and theirs comes with one cutlet and a polite scoop of rice.
shop_smart: The boxed curry roux is the shocker: it eats over 40 percent of this batch on its own. Our Japanese ground beef curry recipe builds the same style of sauce from flour and curry powder for a fraction of that if you want the cheaper route.
Pork chops do katsu duty just as well as pricier cutlets once they are pounded thin, and they cost less per pound. The 6 lb pack keeps the unit price down.
Generic bread crumbs handle the whole crust job for very little. Panko is more authentic and still cheap; use whichever is on sale.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: rinse, simmer covered with water until tender, and set aside.
Pound the pork chops to about half an inch thick and season both sides with salt and black pepper.
Set up a breading line: flour in one dish, beaten eggs in the next, bread crumbs in the third. Coat each chop flour, then egg, then crumbs, pressing so the crust sticks.
Shallow fry in the vegetable oil over medium-high heat, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and 145F inside. Rest on a rack so the crust stays crisp.
Make the curry sauce: bring water to a simmer per the roux package, drop in the curry roux blocks, and stir until dissolved and thick.
Slice the cutlets into strips, portion rice into 14 containers, lay the katsu on top, and ladle the curry alongside so the crust is not swimming in it.
portion_html: Weigh the rice pot and the curry pot, subtract the empty pot number, and divide each by 14, then split the sliced cutlets evenly. Each loaded bowl comes out to about 953 calories and 51 grams of protein.

head.description: Japanese pork katsu curry rice meal prep: 953 calories and 51g protein at about $3.87 a serving (at everyday cost). Crispy breaded pork cutlets with thick curry sauce.
head.keywords: pork katsu curry, katsu curry rice, japanese curry meal prep, breaded pork cutlet, budget dinner recipe
steps: Cook the rice and set aside.
Pound the chops thin, season, and bread them in flour, egg, and bread crumbs.
Shallow fry 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and 145F; rest on a rack.
Simmer the curry roux blocks in water until thick.
Slice the katsu over rice in 14 containers and ladle the curry alongside.
